statement: A top-3 compute jurisdiction legislates guaranteed public access to frontier AI, or an AI dividend or sovereign fund paid to citizens (official gazette, by 2028-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolved. No top-3 compute jurisdiction had enacted such a law by 2026-11-14. In Bloc A the idea moved from think-tank/lab proposals to an introduced federal bill (AI sovereign wealth fund with citizen dividends, June 2026), referred to committee; no floor action found.

items.summary: A top-5 frontier developer published a policy blueprint proposing a public wealth fund giving every citizen a stake in AI-driven growth, with returns distributed directly to citizens.
items.detail: OpenAI, 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First' (April 2026; exact day not verified). Interested party (developer proposing policy about its own sector).

items.summary: A Bloc A senator announced forthcoming legislation for public ownership of half the equity of the largest AI companies via a sovereign fund paying citizen dividends, citing similar proposals by two frontier developers.
items.detail: Sen. Bernie Sanders, New York Times op-ed 'The Public Should Own Half of the Big A.I. Companies' and Senate floor speech (Congressional Record S2467, 2026-06-01), Bloc A. Cites OpenAI public wealth fund and Anthropic sovereign-fund proposals.

items.summary: Bill introduced in the Bloc A upper chamber: one-time 50% equity excise on AI companies with >$200m AI receipts, deposited in a public AI sovereign wealth fund; 5% annual distribution authorised for direct payments to citizens (est. >$1,000 per person). Referred to committee; not enacted.
items.detail: S. 4825 (119th Congress), 'Bloc A A.I. Sovereign Wealth Fund Act', introduced by Sen. Sanders 2026-06-18, referred to Senate Finance Committee (Bloc A). Sponsor estimates fund value ~$7tn.

items.summary: Bloc A executive-branch principal reportedly said the administration supports giving citizens a stake in AI companies but prefers 'pre-distribution' to cash dividends.
items.detail: Tom's Hardware report on VP JD Vance remarks following the Sanders bill (Bloc A). Date approximate; quote not checked against primary transcript.

items.summary: Press reports that a top-5 developer discussed giving the Bloc A government a ~5% equity stake framed as citizens sharing AI upside; no agreement confirmed.
items.detail: Financial Times report on OpenAI discussing a 5% government stake, as cited by Tech Policy Press (Bloc A). FT article not accessed (paywall); date approximate.

items.summary: No enacted statute guaranteeing citizen access to frontier AI or paying an AI dividend was found in any top-3 compute jurisdiction as of the phase end; public-compute programmes elsewhere target researchers and firms, not citizens.
items.detail: Search of congress.gov, OECD.AI policy database and press found only proposals (Bloc A S.4825) and researcher-access compute programmes (e.g. Bloc P sovereign compute, Bloc C AI factories). No Bloc B measure found that guarantees citizen access or dividends.
